question: If the average of P numbers is Q² and the average of Q numbers is P², then the average of (P + Q) numbers will be :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of the first group = P × Q²

Total sum of the second group = Q × P²

Combined sum of both groups = PQ² + QP² = PQ(P + Q)

Average of combined group = Combined Sum ÷ Total Count

Combined Average = PQ(P + Q) ÷ (P + Q) = PQ

**∴ The correct answer is PQ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Average of P numbers = Q²

⇒ Average of Q numbers = P²

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Count = P
 Avg = Q²
 Sum = PQ²

 +

 
 Count = Q
 Avg = P²
 Sum = P²Q

 

 
 Total Count = P + Q
 Combined Avg = Total Sum ÷ (P + Q)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of the first group = P × Q²

⇒ Sum of the second group = Q × P²

⇒ Total Sum of (P + Q) numbers = PQ² + P²Q

⇒ Factoring out PQ from the algebraic expression:

⇒ Total Sum = PQ(Q + P)

⇒ Total Number of observations = P + Q

⇒ Combined Average = PQ(P + Q) ÷ (P + Q)

⇒ Combined Average = PQ

**∴ The correct answer is PQ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Average Formula

When separate groups with given counts and averages are combined, the Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Weighted Average

This type of average attaches a specific weight to each value based on frequency or importance. Formula: Sum(wᵢxᵢ) ÷ Sum(wᵢ).

Deviation Method for Averages

A trick for faster calculation: Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Count). This avoids large multiplications by observing shifts around a central assumed value.
